title.title: One-tape time simulation in two-fifths-power space
title.subtitle: Claim: $T$ steps of a one-tape machine can be simulated in $O(T^{2/5}\,\mathrm{polylog}\, T)$ space

plain: A machine with one tape: replay any run of $T$ steps using only about $T^{2/5}$ cells of scratch memory

panels.caption: one writable tape, one head moving a cell at a time

panels.axisLabel: exponent $e$ in space $T^{e}$ to simulate $T$ steps

beats.text: A machine with one writable tape, run for $T$ steps
The classic simulation uses about $\sqrt T$ space; Williams asked in 2025 to beat it
Claimed: $T^{2/5}$ space, for this model only

achievement.note: One writable tape and a supplied time cap only

verify.detail: No Lean statement; a model-specific manuscript
verify.ourCheck: We did not referee the proof; nothing here is machine-checked

voice.text: Simulating one-tape time in less space.
Last year, time t was shown to fit in root t space. One-tape machines had the same barrier.
Claimed: t to the two fifths space, beating the square root barrier.

sources.quote: Classical O(sqrt t) space simulation for one-tape machines
can be simulated up to a supplied time cap T in O(T^{2/5} polylog T) work space
Model-specific (one writable tape, supplied cap, accessor condition)
